name: pm51-wake-recheck
summary: PM51: wake on port activity only if it is still present 200 ms later (replaces the always-wake stub); keys unaffected

edits.asm: port-wake qualifier stub (called from the wake decision 0x745A for event 2): mov 0x24,#0 -> ljmp 0xA000

bank-0 free space: same scratch writes as the stub; delay_ms(200) via 0x9D2D; re-read PM 0x0386 (bit 5) and 0x038B (bits 2:0), the conditions that raised event 2 in 0x5BAA; r7 = 1 (wake) if any is set, else 0 (stay asleep)

notes: Addresses are PM51 code addresses (bank 0, package offset 0x10080 + addr; executed from flash, covered only by the package CRC). The PM51 uses Keil code banking: common area 0x0000-~0x34FF is identical in bank 0 (0x10080) and bank 1 (0x20080), IRAM 0x1F selects the bank. 0x9D54 and its caller 0x745A are bank-0 code, so the new code is placed in bank-0 space at 0xA000 (0xFF, unreferenced). Whether the PM status bits latch or follow the line is not known: if they latch, this behaves exactly like stock (wake); if they follow the line or clear on read, activity that has stopped after 200 ms no longer wakes the chip. The vendor wake path already uses delay_ms (0x745A calls 0x9D2D(10)). Key events (0x0C-0x15) do not pass through this check.
